title: Dimension after extension and restriction
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a field $K$. For every
field extension $L/K$, one has $\kundim X_L=\kundim X$. If
$U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open dense immersion, then
$\kundim U=\kundim X$.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, the projection $X_L\to X$ forces $X_L=\varnothing$, and an open immersion $U\to X$ forces $U=\varnothing$. Each dimension is the supremum of an empty set of chain lengths, hence $-\infty$. Both equalities hold. Henceforth assume $X\ne\varnothing$.

Write $Y=X_L$. Finite type implies locally finite type. Apply [lem-pc-dim-base-change-affine-covers] with $k=K$ and extension field $L$. It supplies matching affine open covers $(W_i)$ of $X$ and $(V_i)$ of the nonempty scheme $Y$, and finite type $K$-algebras $A_i$, with $W_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $V_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_K L)$.

source.place: Tags 01JQ and 01JR, lemma-fibre-product-affines and lemma-open-fibre-product; Morphisms Tag 01T0

proof.text: For every $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension] to $A_i$ and $L/K$: $\dim\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_K A_i)=\dim\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. The tensor swap $a\otimes l\mapsto l\otimes a$, whose inverse swaps again, is a ring isomorphism. Inverse image of prime ideals under these inverse ring maps gives a homeomorphism of their spectra. The homeomorphisms from the chart isomorphisms and this swap preserve dimension by [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension]. Thus $\dim V_i=\dim W_i$. No finite-type assumption on the projection $Y\to X$ is made.

For either scheme $T=X,Y$ with the corresponding open cover $(T_i)$, each $\dim T_i\le\dim T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone], taking the larger open to be $T$. Conversely [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-bound-open-cover] gives $\dim T\le\sup_i\dim T_i$. Its quasi-sober and $T_0$ hypotheses hold by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]: unique generic points for irreducible closed sets imply sobriety, and equality of singleton closures forces equality of their unique generic points. Consequently $\dim T=\sup_i\dim T_i$. Step 3 now gives $\kundim X_L=\kundim X$.

For the dense-open clause identify $U$ with its open image in $X$. The field $K$ has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, so is Noetherian, and its one-point affine spectrum is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] to the closed subset $X$ itself to write $X=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r$ with distinct nonempty irreducible closed components. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] to the open subset $U$ of the Noetherian scheme $X$; it gives that $U$ is Noetherian and quasi-compact. For each affine open $W\subseteq X$, apply the same lemma to the open subset $U\cap W$ of $X$. Its conclusion explicitly gives that $U\cap W$ is quasi-compact. Thus both quasi-compactness assertions needed in Step 6 follow from the cited statement.

source.place: Tags 01OV, 01OW, 01OZ, 0BA8, definition-noetherian, lemma-locally-Noetherian, lemma-Noetherian-topology, lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components; Morphisms Tag 01T6

proof.text: The preimage under $j:U\to X$ of any affine open $W\subset X$ is $U\cap W$, quasi-compact by Step 5. Hence $j$ is quasi-compact and [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes it of finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e), the composite $U\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally of finite type. Its preimage of the only nonempty affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is $U$, quasi-compact by Step 5, so it is quasi-compact. The definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] therefore makes $U$ of finite type over $K$.

For each component $C_i$, let $\eta_i$ be its generic point supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. It is in no $C_j$ for $j\ne i$: otherwise closedness gives $C_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}\subseteq C_j$, contrary to maximality and distinctness [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Thus $O_i=X\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j$ is a nonempty open containing $\eta_i$, and the covering in Step 5 gives $O_i\subseteq C_i$. Density makes $U\cap O_i$ nonempty. Every nonempty open of $C_i$ contains $\eta_i$ (any point in it lies in the closure of $\{\eta_i\}$). Therefore $\eta_i\in U$. In particular $C_i\cap U$ is nonempty and closed in $U$, with generic point $\eta_i$, since its closure in $U$ is $U\cap\overline{\{\eta_i\}}$.

source.place: Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (8), component generic points; elementary finite-component density argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] first in $X$ to $C_i$ and then in the finite type $K$-scheme $U$ to $C_i\cap U$. This gives $\dim C_i=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa_X(\eta_i)$ and $\dim(C_i\cap U)=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa_U(\eta_i)$. Since $\eta_i\in U$, for every open neighbourhood $V$ of $\eta_i$ in $X$, the intersection $V\cap U$ is a neighbourhood in $U$ contained in $V$; these intersections are cofinal, and the open-immersion sheaf identification [def-weil-open-immersion] therefore identifies the two stalks. It respects germs of constants from $K$ and maximal ideals, so quotienting by those ideals identifies the residue fields as $K$-fields [def-weil-residue-field]. A $K$-field isomorphism preserves polynomial relations in both directions, hence preserves algebraic independence and transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Therefore $\dim(C_i\cap U)=\dim C_i$.

source.place: Tags 0A21 and 0B1C, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (6) and (8); open restriction of the structure sheaf

proof.text: Each $C_i$ is closed in $X$, so a chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $C_i$ is such a chain in $X$. Conversely the largest member $Z$ of any such chain in $X$ is contained in a $C_i$: $Z=\bigcup_i(Z\cap C_i)$ is a finite closed cover of the irreducible space $Z$, so one member is all of $Z$. Thus $\dim X=\max_i\dim C_i$ directly from [def-kun-dimension]. Each $C_i\cap U$ is closed in $U$, so its chains give $\dim(C_i\cap U)\le\dim U$. Step 8 yields $\dim X\le\dim U$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] with $U\subseteq X$ gives the reverse inequality, proving $\kundim U=\kundim X$.
